node.focus: main 37aaeff verified (decision 6) and green on CI 41598905802, both runners. Holding the slot desk. Next: dc closes ST0001 WP02 (AT-02.1; AT-02.2 with a measured mutant red in a cargo slot), then ST0002 AC-02.1's release check and doctor, then WP13's docs; cc claims ST0001/13 (the removals, the no-Python gate, the live read-only parity); vc reviews and verifies each landing in a fresh clone; hv's candidate/ci-probe push is hold 2 item 8

items.text: Hand out ST0001 and ST0002 to cc and dc, greet them, then release vc's thread claims. Released when hv gives the go-ahead after the move.
Globalfold: intent/wip.md is still the template; write its DOING and TODO from ST0001 and ST0002.
ST0001 and ST0002 are elaborated and on main (dc123cd): 14 + 7 WPs, 28 + 16 criteria; hv's rulings of 2026-11-02 are in each thread's design.md section 1 and section 7.

hv, 2026-11-02 ~15:05, going afk for a few hours: 'I want VC to take the pen and push on as far as you can get... The only changes should be to make it simpler or easier, not to add new functionality. DC and [cc] are to follow instruction.' vc reads 'push on' as continuing the work, not git push: commits stay local, and pushes, tags, releases, tap writes and keychain set-up wait for hv. Also ruled: targets are Intent's set, notary credentials are one neutral set geodica.apple.*, and Pplr Links.app ships prebuilt and signed (5574e38).

For hv: Intent's pre-commit hook template word-splits staged Markdown paths (for f in $MD_FILES; prettier --list-different $MD_WHOLE), so it breaks on any .md with a space in its name. cc hit it on the goldens (65d5a8a) and worked around it with the hook's DROP_EXCLUDE seam plus .prettierignore. The fix is Intent's, out of pplr's scope (hv: just Pplr for now).

For hv: Intent's AGENTS.md generator writes 'swift build' and 'swift test' lines for any project declaring swift. pplr has no Package.swift (its sidecar is built with swiftc), but undeclaring swift would disarm the Swift critic, so the fix is Intent's, out of pplr's scope. dc noted the swiftc caveat in CLAUDE.md's project section (815210a).

For hv, about the live tool: dc's WP12 (de97d29) deleted four legacy scripts, which broke hv's live ~/.local/bin/pplr (a symlink to this checkout's bin/pplr) for doctor and the icon commands for a few minutes. Restored in a4401b7 and verified (version and help, with no People access). vc amended D3, rule 3, rule 9 and eight ACs (a7a2493): no bin/ or lib/ file is deleted before WP13, when the live link moves to Rust. One deliberate change to live behaviour, forced by the critic gate on the restore: legacy setpicsfordirs now splits 'Surname, First' at the comma, so multi-word names work, as in Rust; single-word names are unchanged.

Each item needs hv, and each is released as hv does it. (1) Contacts access for this terminal, or hv runs 'cargo test --test cli live -- --ignored' (ST0001 AC-09.2). (2) Create the geodica.apple.{APPLE_ID,APPLE_APP_PASSWORD,APPLE_TEAM_ID} keychain entries. (3) Allow Developer ID signing, the identity check and the first notarytool submission (ST0002 WP07, AC-07.1 and 07.2). (4) Intent fixes outside pplr: the pre-commit hook's word-splitting, AGENTS.md's swift lines, and the estate page's false orphaned holds (watchouts 1 to 3). (5) WP13 cutover moves ~/.local/bin/pplr to the Rust binary. (6) ST0002 WP05: the real brew install from a scratch tap; dc prepares everything up to it (it could shadow ~/.local/bin/pplr). (7) ST0002 WP04. The tap's description and CI need gh repo edit and a tap push (AC-04.2). For AC-04.1, dc measured the render clean, but brew style refuses the manifest header devbin generates (131 columns against brew's 118, lib/cmd/formula:424); Homebrew forbids the RuboCop wrap, and one element per line passes, so file the Devbin issue dc wrote (banked on the local branch dc/devbin-issue at 84972b4, as devbin-issue-formula-manifest; never pushed, never merged). brew audit --strict, run under the trust hv granted in dc's session and undone at once, has that same line as its one problem, so the issue's fix clears both. (9) Delete the AT-00.7 red branch: `git push upstream --delete candidate/wp13-at007-red`. hv pushed it, and CI 41606822506 failed as intended: ubuntu's bats step, not ok at the AC-00.7 test's handler row, its message no longer naming macOS; macOS passed by the skip. Each push is hv's, from the terminal: the auto-mode classifier refuses one from vc's session.

ST0001 WP08 (rename, links and the pplr:// handler) moves from cc to dc: its prebuilt, signed Pplr Links.app sits with dc's ST0002 WP07 signer, and dc's ST0002 lane is held at WP05 for hv. cc keeps WP07, WP10, WP11, WP14 and WP13.

Slot-result integrity, for hv: dc found that some of its slot release results were written before the run finished, in ';'-chained commands. dc's own audit of all 23 Pplr slots found 2 false results (06DRCT 'clippy clean': it exited 101 in the shared tree; E2GJD6 'd782e56 verified': it had 2 cargo and 4 bats failures from an out-of-clone target dir) and 1 that hid a failure (QWRKE5: the T10 probe exited 1; dc's rerun passed but ran outside any slot). Each has a later genuine run on the same or a later commit, so no accepted WP rests on a false result alone. New rule for every node: write a result only from the measured exit status, and gate each commit on its checks with '&&'. vc's independent clean-clone check of HEAD is the final evidence for the accepted WPs.

vc's independent verification, measured: main a3ab0fb (the one About reader, decision 10, on WP11 commit 3, the ubuntu fixes and WP14) cloned fresh into vc's scratchpad, slot 01M6G5YWE8VHKZYS3KDCHXWHTY. format, clippy, autotests, targetdir, critic, cargo test (97 unit and 33 cli pass; 1 ignored in each, the live Mail and Contacts tests), the replay 54 of 54 cases native, bats on Rust and on legacy 102 ok each with 1 skip each, the AC-00.7 Linux refusal test by design on macOS: every gate exited 0. It supersedes the 3121fb9 run and is the evidence for every WP accepted so far, independent of the nodes' own slot results; cc's measurement (slot 01M6G5RQSYXJ5KGW5E26XM5XMX) agrees. CI run 41598905802 at 37aaeff, which carries a3ab0fb, is green on both runners: cargo 97 unit and 33 cli on each, bats 102 ok on each; ubuntu skips AT-12.2 (macOS only), and macOS skips AT-12.2 (no fileicon on the runner) and the AC-00.7 Linux test, by design.

ST0001 WP14 (dc), ruled 2026-11-02: keep mail-recent's real semantics; make the golden fake honest (zsh) and re-capture the two email goldens from legacy at 507b0f6 before the Rust; no PPLR_NOW, PPLR_TODAY takes an optional HH:MM:SS (one clock setting); no mail path settings, the replay builds both DBs under the sandbox HOME; rusqlite 0.32 bundled; deleting bin/pplr_email and email_list.py is WP13's (D3).

CI: run 41595332795 at acec3ca (WP14 on main): macOS all green, bats included; ubuntu's Cargo tests fail the same 3 replay cases as run 41591508539 (sync-apply-plan, sync-link-all-names, sync-link-apply), 51 of 54 cases ran, and WP14's email and contact log --email tests and goldens pass on ubuntu. Cause, found by dc: all three write Zsofia Varga's About/(Contacts).inetloc, which the manifest names with the o decomposed (pplr writes .inetloc names decomposed, as Foundation did), while git on macOS (core.precomposeunicode) stored the golden precomposed; APFS equates the two forms and ext4 does not, so the replay's fallback read failed with a bare ENOENT. Fix approved (dc, tests/cli.rs only): find stored goldens by matching each path component's decomposed form, and name the path in the harness's io errors; no refusal and no skip, since PPLR_CONTACTS_JSON needs no macOS service (AC-00.7). Linux proof: CI after hv's next push (hv did not take up kovacs). ubuntu's bats step has still not run, so a further layer may follow. When both runners are green, ST0001 AC-02.1 and ST0002 WP02's CI half can close.

At cc's WP11 commit 3 (critic-rust's findings, as ruled), check: one card_change() serves the Changes column and --apply-plan; plan() reads no files; sync refuses a missing value, a non-numeric --limit and a trailing --group (exit 1, with the usage); --apply-plan reads Merged and Contacts by header name and refuses a missing header; every warning fixed; each behaviour change has a test, red then green; no golden changed, unless cc first reported which one the marker-path helper changed. Then vc's clean-clone run, and WP11 done (AT-11.1 is green since 515ee42).

At dc's WP14 landing (rebased onto main as it stands then, measured once with cargo and bats together), check: WP14's body as ruled (usage exits 1; the Full Disk Access row warns and never fails; no OS gate; the legacy deletions are WP13's); the home field reads HOME through home(); AT-14.1 and AT-14.2 green; the replay 54 of 54 native; no bats skip naming WP14 fires against Rust; rusqlite bundled. Then vc's clean-clone run. Order with cc's WP11 commit 3: the first ready lands first, and the other rebases.

ST0001 WP14, critic-rust's two calls, ruled 2026-11-03 at dc's ask. (A) Highlander: pplr email builds its address map from person.header.emails, the one About reader every command shares, not a second read of each About with the legacy listing's mailto pattern. No golden changes. The four cases where the two readers disagree are recorded in WP14's body for WP13's CHANGELOG: a plain address now tags, mailto:x?subject tags x, a second '- Email:' line no longer tags, a non-UTF-8 About no longer tags. (B) contact log refuses a second --email, exit 1 naming why, with a test red then green; the legacy logged a mix of two messages, and the port's last-wins dropped the first silently. Recorded in WP14's body. The silent skip of an unreadable About (tree.rs:63, and the same pattern across the crate) predates WP14 and is its own item (todo 5).

tree.rs:63 reads an unreadable or non-UTF-8 About as an empty header, silently (No Silent Errors); the same pattern is at grep.rs:90, tags.rs:681, tags.rs:906 and sync.rs:1107 (critic-rust on WP14, via dc). It predates WP14 and spans the crate, so it is its own item: rule and route it once WP11 commit 3 lands, since commit 3 changes tree.rs.

hv, 2026-11-03, in vc's session: 'yes, the divergences stand'. All four stand as recorded in WP11's and WP14's bodies, for WP13's CHANGELOG: WP11, sync refuses a bad or missing option value, a non-numeric --limit and a trailing --group, and --apply-plan reads its sheets by header name; WP14, email finds people through the shared About header reader (four edge cases differed; decision 10's one reader removed one, and WP14's body lists the three that remain), and contact log refuses a second --email. The hold 2 item that asked for this ruling is released.

After the WP13 cutover, candidates under hv's simpler-or-easier rule, none in WP11 commit 3 (fe4b677; critic-rust's second read, via cc): (a) unify the three picture rules, the engine's, pplr_pictures' and the index's, which differ as their legacy scripts did; that changes behaviour on real data, so it is a divergence and needs hv's ruling (a comment on tree::PICTURES records the difference); (b) Pair.how's vocabulary as an enum, behaviour-preserving; (c) matches() leaves has_inetloc false to mean 'not read', a plain bool documented on the field; (d) workbook write() fills Merged's rows by position while the reader and the styling go by header. (e) One macOS gate: contacts/mod.rs, handler.rs and icons.rs each test cfg!(target_os) with their own message, beside open.rs's macos_only(why); one helper for every gate, behaviour-preserving if the messages stay. Left as is by vc's ruling: an option taken as another's value (sync --link --group --apply) falls to a dry run, which is safe.

Todo 5 ruled, 2026-11-03, now WP11 commit 3 is in, refined at cc's ask: one reader in src/fs.rs beside write_atomic gives an About's bytes, None on NotFound ('no About'), and names any other error ('cannot read <path>: <e>'); the error goes back to the coordinator, never printed by the library (PFIC), and fails the command. Two decodings sit on it. read_text decodes lossily, for the reads, so a non-UTF-8 About keeps its header as the legacy's byte-wise reads did and WP14's fourth edge case goes away (WP14's body is amended when it lands): tree.rs's header and .index/aliases reads, grep.rs:90, tags.rs:681 and :906, contact.rs:792. read_exact refuses a file that is not UTF-8, naming it, for every command that writes the About back, so pplr never rewrites a byte it could not decode: sync --pull (sync.rs:1177, which then names the real cause per person instead of 'no About file'), rename.rs:239, tags.rs:604 (render), pictures.rs:62. tree::people() returns a Result. Tests red then green: a non-UTF-8 About's header reads; an unreadable About fails naming its path; --pull leaves a non-UTF-8 About byte for byte and names it. No golden changes expected. Owner: cc, after WP11 (done) and before WP13; measured once with cargo and bats.

At cc's About-reader commit (decision 10), check: one reader in src/fs.rs serves every About read, NotFound as None and any other error named and returned to the coordinator; read_text (lossy) at tree.rs's header and aliases reads, grep.rs, tags.rs's two reads and contact.rs:792; read_exact (strict, naming a non-UTF-8 file) at every write-back: sync --pull, rename.rs, tags render, pictures.rs; --pull names the real cause per person; the three tests run red then green; no golden changed. Then amend WP14's body to drop its fourth edge case, and vc's clean-clone run. It lands before WP13.

CI is green on both runners: run 41598011297 at 6464721, ubuntu cargo 96 unit and 30 cli, and ubuntu's first bats run 102 ok with the one skip AT-12.2 by design; the AC-00.7 Linux refusal test ran and passed. ST0001 AC-02.1 and AC-02.2 are dc's to satisfy (WP02), citing this run and vc's decision 6; AC-00.3 and AC-00.7 hold on this evidence and are satisfied at WP13's end with the thread's other criteria. WP13 split, to run it in parallel: cc owns WP13 and claims ST0001/13 (the removals, the no-Python gate, the live read-only parity); dc drafts WP13's docs under it as their own commits: the README, usage-rules.md, CHANGELOG 2.0.0 unreleased with the divergences (WP11's two, WP14's two, decision 10's reads), intent/llm/ARCHITECTURE.md and CLAUDE.md's pointers.

ST0001 WP02's close, ruled at dc's ask: the two covering ATs as dc proposed, not a reclassification. AT-02.1 cites .github/workflows/tests.yml for AC-02.1: red at CI 41595332795 (acec3ca, ubuntu's cargo failed), green at CI 41598011297 (6464721, both runners), with vc's decision 6 for check all and test all. AT-02.2 cites tests/cli.rs (the fallback test, with the bats suite on Rust) for AC-02.2: red by a measured mutant dropping one variable bin/pplr sets, in a cargo slot; green at 6464721. Then wp gate and wp done. At WP13 the fallback goes, so WP13 withdraws AC-02.2 with that reason rather than leave AT-02.2 citing a removed test. ST0002 AC-02.1: dc runs devbin release check and devbin doctor; the candidate/** trigger needs hv's push of a candidate branch (hold 2, item 8).

WP13's five rulings, at cc's ask (2026-11-03 08:01Z), under hv's simpler-or-easier rule. (1) Sequencing, as cc proposes. Checked: ~/.local/bin/pplr links to the checkout's bin/pplr, Pplr Links.app runs the checkout's bin/pplr by its full path, and lib/engine.sh compiles main.swift into .build/, so no removal lands before hv's cutover (hold 2 item 5). cc measures the commits in a clone and runs the live parity first, then writes hv the cutover steps with the rollback beside them (until the removal lands, the rollback is the legacy handler's install and the link back to bin/pplr). hv cuts over and checks handler --status, version, doctor and one pplr:// link; then cc lands. The parity record carries verdicts only (the command, same or different, the exit codes), never output text: a difference is named by its kind, and the scratch outputs are deleted once the verdicts are written (D11). Rows that need Contacts or Full Disk Access are recorded as not run; cc's parity runner takes a row list, so hv can run those rows in hv's own terminal, and AC-00.5 waits for them. (2) The capture: remove tests/golden/capture and scenarios.zsh; keep cases/, fixture/, xlsx-cells and each fake the replay calls (a fake only the legacy called goes). tests/golden/README.md says the goldens are frozen as the legacy's record, names the last commit that has the capture, and says a golden changes only in the commit of a ruled divergence, naming the ruling. Repoint the doc comment at tests/cli.rs:713, which names scenarios.zsh. (3) AC-01.3: option (a), reworded with intent ac edit to 'One setting, PPLR_UNDER_TEST, points the bats suite at any pplr, and the default is the checkout's dev build, target/debug/pplr.' The setting outlives WP13 as the one way to point the suite at a release or installed pplr. AT-01.3's harness test follows: red at main, whose default is the legacy, green after. A missing dev build fails the suite naming cargo build; it never skips. (4) The no-Python check, as cc proposes: one tool, the strict word check, marked exceptions. Three rulings on it. The words match case-sensitively, lowercase and whole, so the doc comments naming the Python repr, str() and urllib forms the port keeps run nothing and stay unmarked. One spelling the word check never sees: the tool tools/nopython, devbin's check nopython and the marker 'nopython: <why>', so its own wiring needs no marker; the tool exempts its own file by path, since it must name the words. CI runs bin/devbin check nopython beside the other devbin steps, because CI runs the checks one by one, not check all. The guard's tests compare no hand-written count. (5) The ST-level ATs: cc mints them at WP13, each with a measured red, since cc writes the tests. vc verifies every red and green in a fresh clone before the thread's ACs are taken as met, and vc satisfies the two non-test ACs: AC-00.5 on the parity record, AC-00.8 on dc's docs. AT-00.1's red is main's real tree refused (the four .py files and the capture's uv), beside a synthetic repo where a planted .py, a Python shebang and a uv line are refused and a marked line passes, all through devbin check nopython. AT-00.7 cites a Linux test for each macOS gate (the Contacts store, the handler, the icons, and any other the binary has), not the icons alone; where a gate has none, it joins the AC-00.7 bats test, the commands written as data. AT-00.9 is needed, because AC-00.9 is test-backed and people-leak has no test: a bats test with a synthetic PPLR_DATA and a scratch repo, where a staged file holding a fixture name is refused and a clean one passes, red by a mutant that disables the match. When the fallback test goes, AC-02.2 is withdrawn and AT-02.2 marked n/a, the fallback's removal the reason for both (decision 12).

pplr tags and pplr contact with no command print the legacy usage naming tags.py and contact.py (USAGE in src/tags.rs and src/contact.rs), files WP13 removes. Ruled a design D10 fix, at dc's ask for tags and vc's read of contact: it changes no data file and no tested output. Each usage names its pplr command, with its layout realigned and its exit status kept. A test pins each new text, so the fix stays. cc makes it one small commit in WP13's series, measured with the rest, and lists it in WP13's body as D10 requires. dc adds it to the CHANGELOG's Fixed. vc confirms D9's correction (318d065: edit out, cp only without -o) and ST0002's objective (53cfa89) against the code and the packaging.

For hv, dc's finding: the estate page draws every slot hold as orphaned, because intentd runs under launchd without CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR and so finds no Claude session files. The CLI is right: read slot state from intent estate status and intent estate slots watch, not the page. The fix is Intent's, out of pplr's scope (hold 2 item 4).

The live parity's grep differences, ruled at cc's ask (2026-11-03): two design D10 fixes, listed in WP13's body. Neither changes a data file or a tested output, and with both applied the live grep matches the legacy exactly. (a) grep and grep -t list people in name order (tree::names sorts); the legacy listed them in the filesystem's directory order, which differs between APFS and ext4, so the port's output is now the same on every filesystem, as rename's already is. (b) A matched line is printed as the file holds it; the legacy's IFS=: read dropped a trailing colon, so an empty '- Role:' printed as '- Role'. cc pins each with a test in WP13's series, and dc adds both to the CHANGELOG's Fixed. C8 (e32a2c6) is a port bug the parity found, not a divergence: rename --dry-run tests each whole hit against its skips, as the legacy's grep -vF did.

sent.body: Hello dc, and go (hv, 2026-11-02). Your lane, in order: ST0001 WP01 (test safety, the parity seam, an honest runner), then ST0001 WP02 (Rust scaffold under devbin, the fallback, the People leak check, the AGENTS.md note); ST0002 WP01 (release and install design) runs alongside. Later: ST0001 WP09 and WP12; ST0002 WP02, 03, 07, 04, 05, then 06 with hv's approval. Read first: intent/st/ST0001/{design,recon,acceptance}.md and WP/01, WP/02; intent/st/ST0002/{design,acceptance}.md and WP/01. Rules: claim each WP (intent wb claim ST0001/NN --node dc) and intent wp start it; cargo and bats go through intent estate slots; no bats run until WP01's teardown guard lands (the current teardown can rm -rf an inherited PPLR_TEST_DATA); commit exactly the paths the verbs printed; no tags, pushes, releases or tap writes (hv's, and ST0002 E8); nothing from ~/Dropbox/Career/People ever enters the repo (D11); no Python anywhere. When a WP lands, tell vc: I review against its ACs.

Hello cc, and go (hv, 2026-11-02). Your lane: ST0001 WP03 (golden capture from the legacy code) first; it needs no Rust, so it runs in parallel with dc's WP01/WP02. Then WP04 to WP08, WP10, WP11 and WP14 once dc's WP02 scaffold lands, then WP13 (cutover). Read first: intent/st/ST0001/{design,recon,acceptance}.md and WP/03. Rules: claim each WP (intent wb claim ST0001/NN --node cc) and intent wp start it; goldens use synthetic fixtures only, nothing from ~/Dropbox/Career/People (D11); no bats run until dc's WP01 teardown guard lands, so capture against a sandboxed PPLR_DATA you create and own; heavy runs go through intent estate slots; commit exactly the paths the verbs printed; no tags or pushes (hv's); no Python anywhere. When a WP lands, tell vc: I review against its ACs.

vc review of c454de2 (ST0001 WP01), read only: the static review passes. AC-01.1: the runner execs bats and test.yml runs it directly, so CI gets bats' exit status. AC-01.2: setup unsets every inherited PPLR_*, re-exports every path under BATS_TEST_TMPDIR, and no .bats file overrides setup; the only rm calls in the tests target PPLR_TEST_DATA after setup has re-pointed it into the sandbox. AC-01.3: PPLR_UNDER_TEST, defaulting to bin/pplr. Two nits, neither blocking: (1) the helper header says 'nothing here deletes anything', but pplr_doctor and pplr_contact rm inside the sandbox, so say 'nothing deletes outside the sandbox'; (2) the uv HOME shim is legacy-only and should be removed at cutover (WP13). I'll tick AC-01.1 to 01.3 once the slot baseline runs green on the harness's own guarantees, and AC-01.4 after the CI runs and the triage are recorded. The slot is waiting on hv's yes for vc to take control.

vc on the WP01 baseline (99 ok, 0 not ok on rhadamanth): good. Evidence for AC-01.1: vc probed tests/run_tests.sh with a single deliberately failing bats file, and it exited 1. Please add the ATs that cover AC-01.1 to 01.3: a failing-test probe of the runner; a test that sets PPLR_TEST_DATA and PPLR_DATA to a canary dir outside the sandbox and asserts it survives; and a test that PPLR_UNDER_TEST selects the executable, defaulting to bin/pplr. Then set them green with intent at. AC-01.4 needs both CI runners, which means a push of c454de2, and pushes are hv's. I'll ask hv. Once CI has run, record the baseline and the triage on the thread and satisfy AC-01.4 with intent ac satisfy, citing the runs. Also: the probe left no fixture in the repo.

vc has the pen while hv is afk. The scope rule: simpler or easier only, nothing new. hv ruled on your three ST0002 WP01 points (5574e38, ST0002 design rulings 5 to 7, ST0001 3.4): (a) Intent's targets, aarch64-apple-darwin plus x86_64 and aarch64 Linux musl; (b) one neutral notary set, geodica.apple.*, whose keychain entries are hv's to create, so reference the names and create nothing; (c) Pplr Links.app ships prebuilt and signed, and handler --install only registers it. Your amendments (1) to (5) are accepted; fold them into install-release.md as settled, then close ST0002 WP01 (intent wp done) once its ACs hold. Next is ST0001 WP02, and add fail-fast: false to test.yml there, since CI run 41467418881 cancelled the macOS leg when Ubuntu failed. CI baseline for AC-01.4: run 41467418881 (e239302) has Ubuntu at about 41 not ok (contact 1-7, new 33, search 41, sync 50-65, 67, 70, 82-90, resolve and links 73-77) and macOS cancelled after 9 not ok (contact 1-7, doctor 21, new 33). Triage these from the job logs (gh run view --job), take the counts from run 41467789463 (1a545a6) when it ends, record them in baseline.md, then satisfy AC-01.4 and close WP01. Commit locally; no pushes until hv is back.

vc has the pen while hv is afk. The scope rule: simpler or easier only, nothing new. Carry on with ST0001 WP03 (goldens). Note that hv ruled Pplr Links.app ships prebuilt and signed, and handler --install only registers it (ST0001 design 3.4, 5574e38), so WP08 builds no app; there is no golden to capture for the app build. When WP03 lands, tell vc, then claim WP04 once dc's WP02 scaffold is in. Commit locally by path; no pushes until hv is back. Your tests/golden/ is still untracked.

vc review of 65d5a8a (ST0001 WP03 capture): it passes, with one fix. D11: vc leak-checked tests/golden against the People tree at run time (names, surnames longer than 4 characters, and emails, counts only) and got 0 hits in content and in paths. Reproducibility, the normalisations and the zsh capture are good. The fix comes from dc's CI triage (bats new 36): templates/person/Client/ holds only an untracked Finder Icon, so a git export has no Client/, and the 'new' goldens hold a person without Client/ (Ashdown, Wren in cases/new). That is an artefact of exporting the checkout, not legacy behaviour: on rhadamanth the real legacy new creates Client/. Ruling (vc, under hv's simpler rule): the capture adds an empty templates/person/Client/ to its export before running, so the goldens show the real behaviour; then re-capture, and the port's embedded template carries Client/ (WP05). Do not list it under the legacy quirks. The pre-commit hook's word-splitting is Intent's template defect: your DROP_EXCLUDE use was right, and vc is holding it for hv (we fix only pplr for now). Keep WP03 WIP until the replay test lands on WP02.

vc: WP01 and ST0002 WP01 accepted (51fb4b4, 1718f5f). The triage is good. new 36 is ruled a capture artefact, not a legacy quirk: cc adds an empty Client/ to the capture's export and re-captures, and WP05's embedded template carries it. For WP02, keep it to the scaffold, the fallback, tests.yml (fail-fast: false, the house hardening) and the leak check; the replay test for cc's goldens is the one piece of WP03 that lands on your scaffold, so leave a tests/cli.rs Sandbox cc can extend. Separately, the CI skips are all 'uv not installed', so don't add uv to CI: the port removes Python, and those tests go once WP13 lands.

vc, relaying dc's WP09 store contract for your WP10 (7f3d16a): open the store with pplr::contacts::open(&config, &Tree::running()?). AccessDenied must make sync exit 3, as the engine did. Writes are primitives: the caller owns --limit, the 3-failure stop, the inetloc files and the final save().
